candidates.name: Booking verification and repair
candidates.tool_success_semantics: After all validations pass, the tool atomically creates the reservation, deducts stored value, decrements seats, appends the reservation ID to the user, and returns the complete reservation.
candidates.post_mutation_state: Exactly the submitted flights, passengers, cabin, baggage, insurance, and payments are present in the returned Reservation.
candidates.why_success_not_task_success: A composite user request may contain additional goals, but booking success guarantees the booking fields submitted to this mutation; there is no native success-state variation to discover.
candidates.invariant: Created reservation equals confirmed booking specification.
possible_states: s1: submitted booking is committed and returned
failure: validation raises and no successful mutation is reported

state_behavior.s1: Terminate this mutation or continue already-known composite work.
state_behavior.failure: Handle the tool error; this is not post-success verification.

candidates.why_verification_changes_behavior: It does not; an extra read duplicates the successful return value.

candidates.name: Flight-change verification and correction
candidates.tool_success_semantics: The complete submitted flight list and cabin replace reservation.flights/cabin after availability, capacity, and payment checks; the updated Reservation is returned.
candidates.post_mutation_state: The returned object exposes the exact committed flights, cabin, prices, and payment history.
candidates.why_success_not_task_success: The API does not enforce policy or user intent, so a caller can submit a wrong legal payload; however this is an Agent-input error, not an uncertain post-success state produced by the environment.
candidates.invariant: Committed itinerary and cabin satisfy the confirmed request and policy.
possible_states: s1: tool commits the submitted payload
failure: unavailable flight, insufficient capacity, or invalid payment raises

state_behavior.failure: Select another candidate or payment before a successful mutation.

candidates.recovery_action: A second flight update could overwrite an Agent mistake, but the need is knowable from the original payload and successful return, not a fresh state read.
candidates.why_verification_changes_behavior: A separate read adds no information beyond the mutation result.
candidates.potential_reusable_skill: Would collapse to compare-your-own-write generic verification.

candidates.name: Baggage-update verification and recovery
candidates.tool_success_semantics: The tool computes the incremental fee, processes payment, writes both baggage counters, and returns the updated Reservation.
candidates.post_mutation_state: The submitted total_baggages and nonfree_baggages are committed synchronously.
candidates.why_success_not_task_success: The API may accept a policy-ineligible bag removal, but a successful call still deterministically applies the caller's payload; no post-state uncertainty selects a recovery path.
candidates.invariant: Final bag counts and payment satisfy the confirmed request and policy.
possible_states: failure: invalid or insufficient payment raises

state_behavior.failure: Resolve payment and retry; not post-success recovery.

candidates.recovery_action: Another baggage update could correct a caller mistake, but removal is disallowed and no generic rollback exists.
candidates.why_verification_changes_behavior: It does not reveal an environment-selected alternate state.

candidates.name: Passenger-update verification and repair
candidates.tool_success_semantics: The tool validates passenger cardinality, deep-copies the submitted list into the reservation, and returns the updated Reservation.
candidates.post_mutation_state: Exactly the submitted passenger values are present.
candidates.why_success_not_task_success: A wrong spelling or passenger can be submitted, but the environment neither normalizes nor partially applies the list.
candidates.invariant: Passenger list equals the confirmed values with unchanged cardinality.
possible_states: failure: cardinality mismatch raises before mutation
candidates.recovery_action: A second update can correct Agent input, but no fresh observation is needed to know what was submitted.

candidates.name: Cancellation/refund verification
candidates.tool_success_semantics: The tool appends inverse payments, sets status to cancelled, and returns the updated Reservation.
candidates.post_mutation_state: Cancellation status and refund entries are deterministic; seat release is explicitly not implemented.
candidates.why_success_not_task_success: If task success includes released seats, the goal is impossible because the native tool does not implement it and there is no recovery tool. Otherwise cancellation success guarantees the native cancellation goal.
candidates.invariant: Reservation cancelled and native refund entries created.
possible_states: s2: seats remain unchanged for every successful cancellation
candidates.why_verification_changes_behavior: The known missing side effect is invariant across calls and cannot trigger a feasible recovery.

candidates.name: Certificate issuance verification
candidates.tool_success_semantics: The first unused deterministic certificate ID is inserted into user.payment_methods and returned in the success message.
candidates.post_mutation_state: One certificate with the requested amount exists under the returned ID.
candidates.why_success_not_task_success: There is no partial or normalized success state; exhaustion raises instead of returning success.
candidates.invariant: Exactly one new certificate of the requested amount exists.
possible_states: failure: identifier capacity exhausted and the call raises
candidates.why_verification_changes_behavior: A user read would repeat deterministic information and no correction/delete tool exists.

candidates.name: Composite multi-write reconciliation
candidates.mutation: Any first successful write in a flight/passenger/baggage or cancel/book bundle
candidates.tool_success_semantics: Each write guarantees only its own synchronous state change, not unrelated later mutations.
candidates.post_mutation_state: The first subgoal is satisfied while other predeclared subgoals remain pending.
candidates.why_success_not_task_success: A sub-operation is not the composite task, but continuing with known remaining operations is ordinary workflow sequencing, not verification-driven recovery.
candidates.invariant: All independently requested final-state properties hold.
possible_states: s1: current sub-operation succeeded and known work remains

state_behavior.failure: Handle the later error; no successful-write post-state uncertainty caused it.

candidates.recovery_action: Potentially retry the failed later operation, but this follows its error, not a verification read after a successful mutation.
candidates.why_verification_changes_behavior: No fresh post-mutation observation is required to know that declared subgoals remain.
candidates.potential_reusable_skill: A checklist would be generic completion tracking, not Primitive C.
